item.title: Best accounting firm in France for your business profile
item.description:
In brief:

  1. There is no single best accounting firm in France, but a firm better suited to your business profile. Business leaders can turn to national networks like In Extenso, Cerfrance or Fiducial, or online firms like Dougs.
  2. A startup founder needs support at launch, a tradesman or shopkeeper needs good knowledge of their trade, an SME needs management consulting and solid payroll, an association needs expertise specific to the non-profit sector.
  3. In Extenso, France’s leading independent accounting group, has organized its offer by profile, with dedicated teams for founders, tradesmen and shopkeepers, cafes-hotels-restaurants, professionals, SMEs, agriculture, franchises and associations, across 280 offices.
  4. Cerfrance, historically established with agricultural operators, Fiducial, focused on shopkeepers, tradesmen and professionals, and online firms like Dougs each position themselves on particular profiles.

The best accounting firm in France is the one that best understands your business. A restaurant owner, a doctor, a construction tradesman and the manager of an industrial SME face neither the same obligations nor the same questions. The starting point is therefore your profile. Here is what matters for each and the key players to know.

item.title: Best payroll provider for an SME in France in 2026
item.description:
In brief:

  1. An SME can manage payroll in three ways, in-house with software, by handing payroll to an accounting firm, or with a hybrid solution. The choice depends on the number of employees, collective agreement and need for employment law consulting.
  2. Among the options, accounting firms like In Extenso, Fiducial and Cerfrance offer payroll and social consulting. Software like Payfit offers more independence. Each model suits a different business profile.
  3. In Extenso is among the leading payroll management providers for SMEs in France, with more than 245,000 payslips produced each month and more than 27,000 businesses entrusting it with their social management.
  4. When outsourced, support includes payslips and declarations, social consulting (hiring, contracts, working time, terminations, employee savings) and often employment law assistance.

Payroll is one of the most exposed processes in business. Every month, you must apply the collective agreement, track regulatory changes, calculate contributions which impact the company’s cash flow directly, and transmit the nominative social declaration (DSN). An error affects employee payslips directly and can trigger audits. This is why many business leaders wonder who to trust with payroll. Several options are available to SMEs, from autonomous software to a partner who handles everything. Here are the options and criteria to choose.

item.title: Best support to start a business in France
item.description:
In brief:

  1. There is no single best business creation support, but an ecosystem of actors intervening at different stages of the journey.
  2. Bpifrance Création helps upstream to frame the project, chambers of commerce and craft chambers handle formalities, honour loan networks fund seed stage, and the accountant handles structural choices and follow-up after registration.
  3. On the accounting side, In Extenso supports 8,000 entrepreneurs each year with its dedicated In Extenso Business Creation and Takeover line and a 10-step method, and 90% of businesses it supports survive the first three years.
  4. Combining these actors rather than choosing one reduces the risk of legal structure errors and administrative oversights, and ensures follow-up after registration.

The question of best business creation support rests on a misunderstanding. It assumes one actor covers the entire journey, when reality shows the opposite. Each actor intervenes at a moment in the entrepreneur’s lifecycle, with a distinct expertise.

item.title: Best support to switch to e-invoicing in France
item.description:
In brief:

  1. Best e-invoicing support combines an accounting firm piloting the project and an approved platform executing it technically. Accounting networks, consulting firms and software editors each offer support models suited to the situation.
  2. The firm establishes diagnosis, arbitrates choices and verifies compliance, the approved platform formats the invoice and transmits it. These are two distinct skills, often confused.
  3. Support follows six stages, from scoping diagnosis to platform choice, then configuration, real-world testing, team training and finally gradual switchover.
  4. An approved platform never interprets regulation, it applies the rules it is given. Tax compliance is the firm’s responsibility, not the platform’s.
  5. Skipping the diagnostic stage almost always leads to choosing a platform that does not connect to existing systems, creating double entry.

The most costly confusion over mandatory e-invoicing concerns who does what. A business owner thinks they just need to pick a platform, then discovers nobody is piloting the project. Others think the approved platform decides their tax compliance and are surprised to learn it never does. Best support combines an accounting firm piloting the project and an approved platform executing it technically. Here is how roles and a successful transition really work.

item.title: CFE: understanding the French local business tax
item.description:
In brief:

  1. The CFE is owed by nearly all businesses and self-employed people operating in France as of January 1st.
  2. Its amount depends on the rental value of the property used for the business.
  3. An exemption is possible in the year of creation and sometimes the following year depending on the municipality.
  4. Payment is made online, generally before mid-December.

What the CFE is

The cotisation foncière des entreprises (CFE) is one of the two components of the territorial economic contribution, alongside the value-added contribution (CVAE). It is owed by any individual or legal entity carrying out a non-salaried professional activity in France on January 1st.

item.title: French auto-entrepreneur thresholds 2026: what to know
item.description:
In brief:

  1. The 2026 cap is 188,700 euros for goods sales, 77,700 euros for services.
  2. The VAT exemption applies up to close thresholds; beyond that, the auto-entrepreneur must charge VAT.
  3. Exceeding the cap two years in a row switches the business to the standard sole trader regime.
  4. Revenue must still be filed monthly or quarterly, even with zero income.

The 2026 revenue caps

The French micro-business regime sets annual revenue caps, periodically revised by Urssaf. They differ according to the nature of the activity.

item.title: Getting your Kbis: how to register a company in France in 2026
item.description:
In brief:

  1. The Kbis certificate is obtained online via the INPI single window, typically within 3 to 8 business days.
  2. The ACRE grant offers a partial exemption from social contributions in the first year, under conditions.
  3. Registration costs range from 0 euros for a micro-business to about 250 euros for a company.
  4. A costed business plan makes it easier to access bank financing and public grants.

What the Kbis certificate is and what it is used for

The Kbis certificate is the official identity document of a company registered in France. It certifies its legal existence and states its name, registered address, share capital and the identity of its managers. Any bank, supplier or business client may request it before signing a contract.

item.title: How to read a French payslip line by line
item.description:
In brief:

  1. Gross pay is the basis used to calculate all employee and employer social contributions.
  2. Net pay before tax equals gross pay minus employee contributions only.
  3. Income tax is withheld at source directly on the payslip.
  4. The 2026 French minimum wage (SMIC) sets the minimum reference for any salaried pay in France.

The general structure of a French payslip

A French payslip follows a standardized order since the payslip was simplified: employer and employee identification, gross pay, contributions grouped by risk category, then net pay before and after tax.

item.title: Managing cash flow: the right habits for a small business
item.description:
In brief:

  1. A cash flow forecast updated every week helps anticipate tension before it happens.
  2. Shortening customer payment terms improves cash flow faster than growing revenue.
  3. Factoring provides an advance on unpaid customer invoices, in exchange for a fee.
  4. An incomplete or poorly drafted invoice often delays a customer’s payment by several weeks.

Why cash flow is the first indicator to track

A business that is profitable on paper can still run into trouble if payments come in too late relative to outgoing payments. Unlike accounting profit, cash flow needs to be managed day to day.

item.title: Mandatory e-invoicing: what changes for businesses
item.description:
In brief:

  1. E-invoicing is becoming mandatory step by step for all VAT-registered businesses.
  2. Invoices must go through an approved platform, in a structured format.
  3. The reform aims to simplify tax audits and reduce VAT fraud.
  4. Businesses must adapt their invoicing software or use a dematerialization operator.

The principle behind the reform

Mandatory e-invoicing gradually replaces paper or simple PDF invoices with a structured document sent through an approved platform. The tax authorities’ goal is to gain a near real-time view of transactions between VAT-registered businesses.

item.title: SAS or SARL: how to choose your legal structure
item.description:
In brief:

  1. SAS gives its president an employee-like social regime, SARL puts the majority manager under the self-employed regime.
  2. SASU and EURL are the single-shareholder versions of SAS and SARL.
  3. The self-employed regime costs on average 25 to 30% less in contributions than the employee-like regime.
  4. SAS bylaws can be drafted more freely than SARL bylaws, which are framed by the Commercial Code.

Why the legal structure is a defining decision

The legal structure chosen at start-up determines the manager’s social security regime, governance rules, and by default the company’s tax regime. Changing it later remains possible but involves formalities and costs.

item.title: SCI and LMNP: which taxation for rental property
item.description:
In brief:

  1. An SCI makes it easier to jointly own and transfer a property.
  2. LMNP status allows depreciating a furnished rental property, which sharply reduces taxable rental income.
  3. Real estate capital gains benefit from progressive allowances based on holding period.
  4. The choice between an income-tax SCI or a corporate-tax SCI depends on the wealth strategy pursued.

The SCI, a tool for joint ownership

A société civile immobilière (SCI) lets several people, often family members, jointly own a property through shares rather than direct co-ownership. It eases decision-making and the gradual transfer of wealth through share gifting.

item.title: The role of chartered accountants and regulated liberal professions
item.description:
In brief:

  1. Chartered accountant is a protected title reserved for members registered with the Ordre des experts-comptables.
  2. No general legal requirement forces a small business to use a chartered accountant.
  3. A regulated liberal profession follows practice and ethics rules set by an order or authority.
  4. Self-employed nurses, for example, combine standard accounting obligations with rules specific to their professional order.

What a chartered accountant actually does

A chartered accountant is a professional registered with the Ordre des experts-comptables, the only one entitled to use that title. They keep or supervise a business’s accounts, prepare its annual financial statements, and advise on tax, social or management choices, under a precise professional and ethical liability.
